colors.name: newsprint
colors.role: the page ground — cheap newsprint cream; every photocopy tone is set against it

colors.name: stock
colors.role: taped-on photos & pull quotes — a half-step brighter, like glossy paper pasted onto newsprint

colors.name: ink
colors.role: primary text, headlines, halftone dots, the masthead (14.6:1 on newsprint)

colors.name: ink-soft
colors.role: secondary text — captions, folios, marginalia, deks (8.7:1 on newsprint)

colors.name: highlighter
colors.role: DECORATIVE ONLY — the neon-yellow highlighter stroke behind pull quotes & flagged words, tape strips. Never carries text on its own (2.3:1 as text — swatch is 14.8:1 as ink-on-yellow but text stays ink).

colors.name: highlighter-ink
colors.role: ink set over the highlighter swatch — pull quotes and flagged words read as ink-on-yellow (14.8:1), the highlighter is the marker, not the ink

colors.name: stamp
colors.role: the rubber-stamp red — folio numbers, the POSTAGE stamp, the ‘NO GODS / NO MASTERS’ stamp, focus ring. Used sparingly like a hand-inked seal (5.7:1 on newsprint as text, large-weight only)

colors.name: rule
colors.role: column rules & borders — solid ink hairlines that hold the dense grid together; 1–2px only

fonts.role: condensed Latin display — masthead, headlines, folios, kickers, the marquee band; the poster voice
Korean serif & structural body — every Hangul glyph (the masthead 잡지, all essays, marginalia), Korean-first running text at weight 400/500/700/900

texture: Photocopy energy, built from layering, not files. (1) Halftone-dot photos — CSS radial-gradient dot fields inside masked panels, density tuned so they read as newsprint halftone, never as a real raster. (2) Tape strips — translucent cream rectangles at low opacity (0.5–0.7) rotated ±3–6°, holding photos and pull quotes like masking tape on a collage. (3) Highlighter marks — solid yellow bars behind pull quotes and single words, slightly rotated and oversized like a real marker pass. (4) Rules — 1–2px ink hairlines everywhere: column rules, masthead rules, picture-frame borders. (5) Misregistration — photos and tape sit ±1–3° off-axis, the whole grid leans into being handmade. No feTurbulence, no image noise filters — the grain is geometric.

motion.name: ease-punk
motion.value: cubic-bezier(0.2, 0.8, 0.2, 1) — clip wipes & letter reveals: snappy in, slight settle, never precious

motion.name: ease-stamp
motion.value: cubic-bezier(0.34, 1.56, 0.5, 1) — the stamp drop: ~6% overshoot, like a stamp pressed too hard

motion.name: clip wipe
motion.value: inset(0 100% 0 0) → inset(0 0 0 0), 760ms ease-punk; diagonal variant polygon(0 0,0 0,0 100%,0 100%) → polygon(0 0,100% 0,100% 100%,0 100%)

motion.name: letter reveal
motion.value: per-glyph: opacity 0→1 + translateY(0.5em) + rotate(-4deg) → 0, 90ms + 45ms×i stagger, 480ms ease-punk

motion.name: marquee drift
motion.value: base 0.05 px/ms (~50 px/s); rAF translate3d wrap, dt-normalized; reversed & boosted by scroll direction/velocity (dir·−speed, +0.04·vel, cap 0.32); idle stills under reduced motion

motion.name: marquee wrap
motion.value: offset kept in (−w,0] across 4 identical groups so the seam is invisible

motion.name: reveal
motion.value: 560ms ease-punk, translateY(16px) → 0 + opacity, 70ms stagger per observer batch

motion.name: halftone reveal
motion.value: radial-gradient bg-position eased 900ms ease-punk so dots ‘develop’ like a darkroom print on the clip wipe
